rule: Watch idle window and remediation-cycle floor
description: P3 coupling. The watch budget is an IDLE window re-armed per completed remediation cycle, not an absolute total budget, and the cycle cap is a floor that no caller may undercut. The source pin sits on ONE span carrying BOTH halves of the idle rule: the positive half (a completed remediation cycle re-arms a fresh full window) and the terminating half (a window that elapses with no actionable arrival ends the watch). Pinning only one half leaves the other rewritable -- dropping the re-arm silently reverts `max_watch_duration` to a total budget that expires mid-review, and dropping the elapse clause removes the only stated exit -- so both live inside the pinned span. The consumer pin on `plugin/agents/overlord.md` is a POINTER-TO-ENFORCEMENT pin, not a number pin: the floor's VALUE is not the caller-boundary contract and is not stated at the caller at all. The value is declared and enforced in `plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/loop-state.sh` and is pinned there by `tests/policy/safety-cycle-floor-single-source.json`. What IS the caller-boundary contract, and what this pin holds, is the conjunction the overlord sentence states in one span: that a floor exists, that the named script REJECTS any lower `max_remediation_cycles`, and that no caller may invoke this loop with a lower value. Rewriting the reference away, or dropping the no-lower-value obligation, turns the suite red; per rule 3 of the pin-authoring contract the prose around those words stays free to be reworded. What this fixture honestly guarantees is exactly that these two word sequences exist in these two named files; it claims nothing about meaning and nothing about runtime behavior. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a static pin CANNOT prove the re-arm actually happens at runtime -- it proves only that the contract text is present, and an implementation that arms Monitor once with a total deadline stays green; (2) the sentence that follows the pinned span in the skill (the poll script's deadline being per-process) is deliberately OUTSIDE the pin so it stays rewritable, and deleting it alone stays green; (3) the default-value table row carrying `3600` is unpinned, so a changed default is invisible; (4) this fixture holds the overlord's POINTER only -- the floor's declaration and its enforcement guard are out of its reach and are covered by the single-source fixture named above, so a floor lowered inside the script is invisible HERE; (5) the pin sees only the two files it names, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW caller that invokes the loop without honoring the floor -- that is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract and needs a structural check, not a presence pin.

source.pattern: `max_watch_duration` is an IDLE window, not a total budget: a completed remediation cycle re-arms a fresh full window, and a window that elapses with no actionable arrival ends the watch.

consumers.pattern: `max_remediation_cycles` is a FLOOR declared and enforced by `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/loop-state.sh`, which REJECTS any `max_remediation_cycles` below it: no caller may invoke this loop with a lower value.
